items.uk-ai-5-principles::principle-1-safe: AI should be safe, secure and robust by design, with appropriate fail-safes and the ability for humans to intervene in decisions the system shapes.
items.uk-ai-5-principles::principle-2-appropri: Organisations using AI should be able to explain what it is doing and take responsibility for its outcomes, with transparent processes and clear accountability mechanisms.
items.uk-ai-5-principles::principle-3-fairness: AI systems should be fair and just, with attention to bias, discrimination and equitable treatment across different groups in design, data and outcomes.
items.uk-ai-5-principles::principle-4-transpar: It should be clear when AI is being used, how decisions are made, and what the limitations of the AI system are.
items.uk-ai-5-principles::principle-5-accounta: Existing regulators should proactively adapt and apply existing principles-based approaches to AI in their remits, so that accountability for AI outcomes is clearly assigned, including for fairness of decisions AI shapes.
